applies_why: The judge text uses a single verse's admission of two readings as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand: reading 1, two admitted readings make UNDERDETERMINED; reading 2, two senses are not open and both stand. I weighed whether 'admits both readings' is an openness finding or a forbidden ground.
why: The judge made the verse's admission of two readings the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which the rule forbids because both senses stand and the verse is not open.
